subject: Glacier Systems — commercial terms: commit floors, true-up cadence & burst protection
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@glaciersys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@glaciersys.com
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RFP — clarification on commercial section (commits / overages)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP packet — we're reviewing the technical appendices now. A few procurement items need clarification in the commercial/pricing section before our procurement committee will accept the redlines:

- Please confirm how token unit pricing maps to generation vs. embedding calls (we have two distinct workloads). Are those priced separately or blended?
- For a multi-year commit, how do you amortize the committed spend for invoicing and for early termination refunds?
- What's the proposed true-up cadence? We typically do annual true-ups but are open to semi-annual.
- We need clarity on burst protections: if our usage spikes above commit in Q1, what credits / graceband do you recommend for enterprise customers?
- Can you provide at least one sample invoice calculation showing commit allocation, overage calculations, and applied credits/discounts?

If you can send a short commercial appendix back (1–2 pages) plus a pricing matrix, procurement can complete their review in the next week.

Attachment: Glacier_RFP_Q3_v2.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Glacier Systems
elena@glaciersys.com
Phone: +1 206 555 0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP — clarification on commercial section (commits / overages)

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the checklist. See below for a concise commercial appendix and a worked invoice example; I attached a pricing matrix for the deal as well (CSV) and a short summary PDF of commit terms. If you want, we can convert these into the contract SOW markup for redlines.

High-level commercial response (summary):

1) Unit pricing & workload separation
   - Generation (text completion/chat): baseline listed price $0.00090 / token for on-commit consumption.
   - Embeddings (vector generation): baseline listed price $0.00075 / token on-commit.
   - Off-commit overage pricing is a premium above baseline (see tiers below). We price generation and embeddings separately due to cost profile differences.

2) Commit tiers & discounts (example annualized tiers):
   - Tier A: 0–1B tokens / month committed — baseline unit prices above; no additional volume discount.
   - Tier B: 1B–3B tokens / month — 8% off baseline unit price.
   - Tier C: 3B+ tokens / month — 15% off baseline unit price.
   - Committed monthly quantity is pooled across product routes by default unless customer requests per-route accounting.

3) Overages, burst cushions & gracebands
   - Standard overage rate (applies after commit exhausted within a billing period): 1.33x baseline per-token rate for that workload (e.g., generation overage = $0.00120 / token).
   - Graceband: 10% monthly buffer applied before overage billing is enforced.
   - Burst cushion (enterprise add-on): For multi-year deals we can include a burst credit pool equal to 20% of average committed monthly tokens for the first 3 billing months. These are consumed before overage billing.

4) True-up cadence & amortization
   - Default true-up: annual, aligned to contract anniversary.
   - Optional semi-annual true-up available for larger customers (adds modest admin fee).
   - Amortization: committed annual dollars are amortized evenly across 12 monthly invoices by default; overages are invoiced monthly.

5) Early termination & refunds
   - Early termination refund: pro-rata unused committed dollars minus a 10% administrative wind-down fee, subject to minimum 90-day notice.

6) Example invoice (monthly) — worked example
   - Committed monthly quantity: 1,200,000,000 generation tokens; 200,000,000 embedding tokens
   - Amortized committed spend (generation): 1.2B * $0.00090 = $1,080,000
   - Amortized committed spend (embeddings): 0.2B * $0.00075 = $150,000
   - Actual usage month: generation 1.45B tokens, embeddings 0.22B tokens
   - Generation overage = (1.45B - 1.2B - graceband) * overage rate. Graceband of 10% on generation commit = 120M tokens buffer. Overage billed = 1.45B - 1.2B - 120M = 130M tokens * $0.00120 = $156,000
   - Embedding overage = similar calculation (applied embedding overage rate)
   - Applied burst credits (if enabled): first three months, up to 20% of committed monthly tokens for workload — consumed before overage billing.

Attachments: glacier_pricing_matrix_v3.csv (CSV), redwood_commit_terms_summary.pdf (PDF)

Next steps: I can prepare a concise commercial exhibit for your legal team with explicit SOW line items and invoice examples for inclusion in the contract. If Glacier prefers semi-annual true-ups or a different graceband, we can model the invoice effect and update the matrix.

Thanks — looping in Karthik to confirm any optional SLA credit language and Jordan for billing flow notes.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Glacier Systems — commercial terms: commit floors, true-up cadence & burst protection

Marissa / Priya —

Quick internal thoughts to consider for the exhibit we'll send to Glacier:

- Consider a blended per-token cap for customers that heavily mix embeddings and generation; provide an optional blended band that sits between the two baseline rates to simplify invoicing. Gives procurement one line item to compare against peers.
- Propose an escrow-like overage credit for year-one only: customer prepays 2% of annual committed spend into a reconciliation pool that covers administrative true-up friction. Unused funds are credited back at true-up.
- SLA credit: offer a 60-day credit pool (percentage of monthly committed spend) triggered after repeat latency violations — this helps close procurement objections without changing base economics.

I'll draft wording for the commercial exhibit (short bullets + sample invoice) and drop it into the HubSpot deal.

-Karthik

Marissa —

Thanks for the comprehensive appendix and the worked invoice. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups but overall directionally this looks good. Two notes from our side:

1) Glacier would like the burst cushion for the first two quarters instead of three (we expect seasonal peaks but want to limit extended credits). Can Redwood adjust that in the draft exhibit?
2) We prefer annual true-ups aligned to our fiscal year (July 1). Please include a sample true-up statement that references an annual reconciliation on July 1 with any net overage invoiced within 30 days.

If those two changes are reflected, procurement is prepared to move to legal for a contract markup and would expect DocuSign-ready exhibits by next Tuesday. Please send the DocuSign link when ready.

Best regards,
